attribution.note: The forecast is Listgarten's, but Marcus adopts it in his own voice with 'I couldn't agree more'. The 'parallel arguments' sentence is his own words.

semantics.note: The adopted 'will not, anytime soon' is an unqualified negative forecast with no deadline. The 'could be made in many domains' part only states a possibility, so it is correctly kept as a qualifier and is not scored.

contract.note: The plain reading of 'virtual scientists' (investigations producing valid new findings, not just literature synthesis) is ordinary and fair. The contract correctly refuses to borrow the end-2025 deadline and allows early contradiction only on an unambiguous event.

evidence.note: Sakana's description of its own work: end-to-end generated papers, human selection, workshop scores, paper withdrawn. It does not independently validate any finding.
Independent evaluation of the earlier AI Scientist found hallucinated results and failed experiments. It does not settle what later systems can do.
Kosmos preprint by its developers. Expert corroboration happened inside the developers' own study, with objectives and datasets supplied by scientists. Not an unambiguous independent validation.
Peer-reviewed Nature report of the AI Scientist system. Its benchmark is passing the first round of workshop review, not independent verification of a novel finding.

reviews.rationale: 'Anytime soon' sets no deadline. The candidate counterexamples (Sakana, Kosmos, the Nature AI Scientist paper) do not show an unambiguous, independently validated autonomous discovery, so the early-resolution rule is not met. Reaching the evaluation date cannot count as support. Unresolved.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: This is a judgment about April 2024 capabilities across the whole listed set. 'Seem' softens it, and the proposition keeps that softening ('appear'). It is a tentative observation, not a probability forecast.

contract.note: Using April 1–12, 2024 as the window, keeping each task's own requirements, and letting one complete task contradict 'all' is an ordinary reading. Many quality standards ('engaging', 'award-caliber') are unspecified, so interpretation drives the result.

evidence.note: April 2024 study showing factual drift in generated biographies. Consistent with the claim, but not a comprehensive negative finding about biography writing.
DARPA's own account of RACER off-road autonomy from late 2023, including creek crossings. It does not show driving without maps, so it does not meet the task as stated.
Mobile ALOHA learned specific household tasks from demonstrations. That is not working in random kitchens or cleaning unfamiliar homes.
The Nobel announcement credits human researchers for AlphaFold2. It does not show the AI originated a discovery on its own.

reviews.rationale: No item shows a complete listed task done under its stated requirements during the window: RACER lacks the no-maps condition, and Mobile ALOHA lacks the unfamiliar-home condition. The support condition is also unmet, because there is no comprehensive assessment across all tasks. The evidence does not settle it.
